The structure should be designed to be well insulated in the ceiling, walls, and floor, and so that it can be well ventilated to take advantage of cooling summer breezes. Further, the San Jose area has the advantage of being a good locality for utilizing solar energy for heating needs (both space heating and water heating). Some solar collectors are also useful in the cooling of the structure during the summer.
The demolition and clearing operations in the Mayfair and Gardner neighborhoods will require the energy for the destruction, removal and disposal of materials. In all likelihood, the land so cleared would be again available for new construction. Thus, as an indirect effect, energy would be utilized for the manufacture, transportation and placement of the materials utilized in the new structure. Further, the new structure would present its own gas and electric demands, presumably for residential uses. These long-term demands for energy could be less than the demands of the structure which was removed if the more stringent insulation requirements are followed and if energy efficient design is emphasized.
The street improvement program in the Alviso, Northside, and Gardner areas will involve the energy necessary to excavate and haul away unuseable portions of the existing pavement, curbs, gutters, and stormdrains. In addition, new materials must be processed, transported, and placed to create safe and useable streets.
The Alviso clean-up program will involve the energy required for the collection and disposal of the material (glass, litter, scrap metal, garbage, etc.) which is collected. This is a relatively minor amount of energy and does not represent any continuing demand. To the extent that collected material is recycled, there will be a positive net impact.
The construction of curb ramps for the handicapped will involve a one-time expenditure of energy of a relatively minor nature.
